title: How Soon Can You Assign an Off-Plan Contract? A Realistic Timeline
seoTitle: How Soon Can You Assign an Off-Plan Contract?
description: In my experience, assigning an off-plan contract at a profit takes 24 to 36 months, but some projects take far longer. How to plan for it.
answer: In my experience, 24 to 36 months from signing is a reasonable time to assign an off-plan contract to a new buyer at a profit. But some projects take four, five, six or even eight years, which is why checking the developer's history is essential.
body:
One of the most common questions I get: how soon can I assign my contract?

## The usual window

Based on my experience, **24 to 36 months** is usually a reasonable time to assign a contract to somebody else with a profit. By then the building is visibly rising, the risk has dropped, and the gap between your price and the market price has had time to grow.

## The exceptions are long

I have also seen projects take four, five, six, even eight years. Permits get stuck, financing falls through, construction stops and restarts. During that time your money is tied up, and you may still owe deposits at each milestone.

## Plan for the long case

If your plan only works when everything goes on time, it is not a plan. Ask yourself whether you can keep paying the deposits and wait if the project takes twice as long as promised.

## Check the developer's history

The best way to estimate the real timeline is to look at what the developer did before:

- How many projects have they finished?
- How late were they compared with the dates they announced?
- Did any project stall or get cancelled?

A developer's rate of success on past projects is the most honest forecast of your timeline.

## Check the contract too

Some contracts limit when you can assign, for example only after a certain share of units is sold or only with the developer's approval. Read that clause before you sign.
takeaways: 24 to 36 months is a common window to assign at a profit.
Some projects take four to eight years, so plan for delays.
A developer's past delivery record is the best timeline forecast.
Read the assignment clause: some contracts restrict when you can assign.
faq: Can I assign my off-plan contract right after signing?
Sometimes, but there is usually little profit that early, and some contracts forbid assignments until a share of units is sold or construction reaches a certain stage.
What happens to my deposits if the project is delayed?
They stay committed, and you may still owe milestone payments. Check what the contract says about delays and refunds.
How do I know if a developer delivers on time?
Compare the completion dates they announced for past projects with when those buildings were actually finished.
